bindings.title: Select the Google Sheets documentId
bindings.detail: The dropdown shows "Task Tracker", which is a placeholder label with no value behind it - the node looks configured and is not. Open Record Uptime Metric and pick the real documentId from the list.

behaviour.title: Replace the Twilio sender number
behaviour.detail: The from number is +15550100000, which is in the reserved fictional 555-01xx range and is not a number anyone can send from. Twilio rejects it. Put a number on your own account here, or a Messaging Service SID.

behaviour.title: Set a real fallback for the placeholder expressions
behaviour.detail: "ONCALL_NUMBER" appears as the fallback branch of an expression. When the upstream field is missing the expression does not fail - it resolves to that literal string and the call is made with it, which reads downstream as a malformed value rather than as missing data.

behaviour.title: Point the HTTP calls at your own endpoint
behaviour.detail: The URLs "service-a.example.com", "service-b.example.com" are illustrative - example.com is reserved for documentation and resolves to nothing useful. Replace them with the service you are actually calling, and set that service's authentication on the node.

behaviour.title: Clear the pinned sample data before going live
behaviour.detail: "Receive Inbound Webhook" carries pinned sample data, which is what lets the workflow run end to end before you have wired anything up. While it is pinned, a manual execution reads the sample and never calls the real service - so the run succeeds and proves nothing about your setup. Unpin it once the credentials and bindings are in place.

bindings.title: Import "lib: Post-Process Metrics" and select it on Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
bindings.detail: This template calls a separate workflow named lib: Post-Process Metrics, and it is included in your download as lib/lib-post-process-metrics.json. Import that file into n8n first (Workflows -> Import from File), then open Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow and pick it in the workflowId selector. The selector is empty until you do: a workflow id only exists inside your own instance, so it cannot be set for you.

behaviour.title: Calendar events go to your own primary calendar
behaviour.detail: The Google Calendar nodes are set to "primary", which Google resolves to the default calendar of whichever account you connect. That is why this template runs as imported rather than failing on an unset dropdown. If these events belong on a shared or team calendar, change the Calendar field on the nodes below from "primary" to that calendar.
